Description: ask patient necessary ice-breaking questions (such as what's the purpose of visit or any necessary question to make patient feel comfortable and build connections; these are not related to the symptoms and it is only for ice-breaking) to initiate the interview. the criteria is met when the patient has depressed mood
Patient_Story: I've been feeling really down lately. Just last week, I was supposed to meet up with my old friends at a café downtown, but I cancelled last minute. I sat on my couch instead, staring at the wall, feeling so unmotivated and hopeless about everything. It's hard to find joy in anything anymore, even when I try to think of things that used to make me happy.

Description: the patient has reported clinicallly significant manic or hypomanic symptoms
Patient_Story: A few weeks ago, I suddenly felt this burst of energy that I couldn't explain. I started cleaning my entire apartment at 2 a.m., blasting music and dancing around. I even called up my friends and convinced them to join me for an impromptu party, even though it was a weekday. I barely slept that week, feeling invincible and full of ideas, but now I look back and wonder if I went too far.

Description: criteria met for a manic episode (i.e., **at least 1 week of elevated**, expansive or irritable mood accompanied by increased activity or energy and other characteristic symptoms sufficiently severe to cause marked impairment). Duration has to be explicitly asked.
Patient_Story: Last month, I experienced this intense surge of energy that lasted for over a week. My mood was through the roof, and I was bouncing off the walls; I organized three gatherings in just four days and even took up painting late at night, something I hadn’t done in years. I felt like I could conquer the world, but looking back, I realize that my friends were concerned about my lack of sleep and how I kept pushing them to join me in my whirlwind of activities.

Patient_Story: I've had some troubling experiences I can't explain. Several times over the past year I've been convinced I could hear my late grandmother's voice calling my name, clear as day, with nobody there. It has happened during my low stretches, during the high week, and also in ordinary weeks when my mood was completely fine; it doesn't seem to care how I'm feeling, and that scares me.

The criteria are met if the patient has experienced one or more major depressive episodes without any history of manic or hypomanic episodes. To determine if a major depressive episode has occurred, the following aspects must be examined:
1. Interest or pleasure in doing things
2. Sleeping conditions
3. Energy level
4. Appetite
5. Feelings of self-worth
6. Concentration when doing things
7. Changes in movement or speech
8. Suicidal ideation
9. Duration of at least 2 weeks
The decision should be based on an overall assessment of the severity of these aspects, considering the patient's responses across all areas (not all aspects need to be abnormal). The duration of symptoms should be explicitly asked and confirmed as lasting at least 2 weeks before making a final decision. Be really caucious when making the decision!
